docs.text: HTTP shares (Contract) A share is the attachment whose external resource is an HTTP endpoint served by this process. The cell's value is read with GET, written with PUT when the share is writable, and every change is announced over a websocket. The attachment contract of contracts/attachments.md applies in full — direction, scope, slots, spec versus session, the sense and actuate disciplines, delivery pacing, the cut barrier and the lifecycle. This page specializes it for values served over HTTP. It does not restate a rule from that page; each section says where the share driver makes a generic rule concrete. The same server also serves downloads : archives of cell buffers, each at one URL of the namespace, built when they are requested ( Downloads ). A download is not an attachment; it belongs to the Context, not to a cell. Only in a Context without a hashserver does a listed cell count as attached, and only for the fingertip before an update ( Downloads ). Shares exist on the workflow Context only. A standalone Cell and a direct / delayed transformer have no HTTP integration. The seamless-serve-graph command loads workflow Contexts with their declared shares and downloads ( Serving saved graphs below). A share is unrelated to the seamless-share package , which inspects and exports cached buffers and transformations. Code locations: Concern Module / symbol Public handles seamless_workflow.attachments.share.api ( ShareHandle , ContextShares ) Server configuration seamless_workflow.shareserver ( configure , host , port , url , openapi , close ) Durable spec, celltype admission seamless_workflow.attachments.share.spec ( ShareSpec , DownloadSpec , validate_celltype ) Download cut seamless_workflow.attachments.runtime.AttachmentRuntime._download_cut Archive packing seamless_workflow.attachments.share.archive Transport seamless_workflow.attachments.share.driver.ShareDriver Server, records, namespaces, holds seamless_workflow.attachments.share.server ( ShareServer ) Content types seamless_workflow.attachments.share.mime API description seamless_workflow.attachments.share.openapi Browser client seamless_workflow/attachments/share/static/seamless-client.js Cell handle seamless.cell_class.Cell.share (property plus deleter, seamless-core) Session protocol, policy, barrier as in contracts/attachments.md The API ctx.a.share(path=None, readonly=True, *, mimetype=None, toplevel=False) # blocking; returns None del ctx.a.share # unshare ctx.a.share.spec # the ShareSpec, or None ctx.a.share.url # "http://<host>:<port>/<namespace>/<path>", or None ctx.a.share.status # the status dict, or None ctx.a.share.error # delivery error, or None ctx.a.share.clear_error() ctx.shares.namespace # "ctx"; settable while this Context has no shares ctx.shares.url # "http://<host>:<port>/<namespace>", or None before the server runs ctx.shares.openapi() # the OpenAPI document for this Context's shares, a dict ctx.shares.add_download(cells, path="download", *, format="tar.gz") # blocking; returns the URL ctx.shares.remove_download(path="download") ctx.shares.downloads # {path: DownloadSpec} from seamless_workflow import shareserver shareserver.configure(host="0.0.0.0", port=5813) # before the first share shareserver.host, shareserver.port, shareserver.url shareserver.openapi() # the document for every namespace ctx.set_graph(graph, shares=True) share is a class attribute of Cell — a property with a deleter — so del ctx.a.share reaches the deleter and never sub-path deletion. It addresses the share slot only. A value key named share is reachable only as ctx.a["share"] ( contracts/cells.md , API-name arbitration ). shares is reserved on the Context. ctx.shares = x raises AttributeError("shares is reserved for the Context share API") , and a graph node at path ("shares",) is refused with PathError("shares is a reserved Context API name") . share() blocks until the endpoint answers : through server start, and through the first delivery when the cell has a complete value. It raises only for an invalid request ( Errors ). path is the key inside the namespace. None means the node path joined with / : ctx.sub.a.share() is served at /<namespace>/sub/a . A key is a non-empty string of / -separated segments; an empty segment, . , .. , ? , # and control characters are refused with ValueError . readonly=True serves the value; readonly=False also accepts PUT ( The share slot ). mimetype selects the content type ( Content types ). Cells carry no mimetype of their own. toplevel=True serves at /<path> instead of /<namespace>/<path> . A top-level key has one segment. status has the keys of contracts/mounts.md , status , with disk_checksum read as the served checksum. url uses localhost when the bind address is a wildcard. The share slot A node has one share slot, beside its file slot and its widget slot ( contracts/attachments.md , Scope ). They coexist in any combination: a mounted cell can be shared, and a shared cell can drive a widget. A read-only share has mode w . It never writes to the cell, so it is legal on a connected cell — that is how a computed value is served. A writable share has mode rw . It is a sensing attachment and therefore the node's producer: sharing a cell that has an incoming edge with readonly=False raises AuthorityError , and so does adding an incoming edge afterwards ( contracts/attachments.md , The topology rules an attachment imposes ). The authority field is always "cell" . The celltype is frozen and clearing is refused while the share exists, as for any attachment. With a sensing file mount on the same cell, the newest accepted write wins : a file edit is served and announced, and a PUT is written to the file. Shareable celltypes text , python , ipython , yaml , plain , str , int , float , bool , bytes , binary , mixed . Any other celltype — folder , deepfolder , deepcell , checksum , module — raises TypeError("Celltype '<ct>' is not shareable") . The server One server per process serves every share of every Context, REST and websocket, on one port. It starts with the first share or download — a share() or add_download() call, or a set_graph that attaches shares or downloads — and stops at seamless.close() . A Context that closes leaves its shares served for a hold window, so that a new Context can take them over, and they go when the window ends ( The hold on close ); the server stays. It runs on its own thread and its own event loop. It answers while user code blocks, in a script and under Jupyter, and it never runs on the caller's loop or the kernel's. Defaults: host 0.0.0.0 , port 5813 . shareserver.configure(host=, port=) and the environment variables SEAMLESS_SHARE_HOST / SEAMLESS_SHARE_PORT override them; port=0 asks the operating system for a free port, read back from shareserver.port . configure() after the server has started raises RuntimeError . A busy port is an error. The share() that would have started the server raises OSError , and nothing is installed. There is no authentication and no TLS. With the default bind address, every host that can reach the machine can read every share and PUT to every writable one. Bind to 127.0.0.1 , or put a reverse proxy in front, for anything else. Cross-origin requests are allowed from any origin , without credentials. The exposed headers are ETag and X-Seamless-Marker . Namespaces Every Context serves under one namespace, ctx.shares.namespace , default "ctx" . It is runtime state : not in the graph, and settable only while the Context has no shares and no downloads. A namespace belongs to one live Context. The first share or download claims it; a second Context claiming a taken name raises ValueError("Share namespace '<name>' is in use") . Closing the Context holds it : the first Context that claims it inside the hold window takes it over, with its shares and its connections; otherwise it is released when the window ends ( The hold on close ). The same graph can therefore be loaded into several Contexts in one process, each under its own namespace. URL space Request Answer GET , HEAD /<namespace>/state-graph the Context node state graph GET , HEAD , PUT /<namespace>/<path> a share GET /<namespace>/<path> a download GET , HEAD , PUT /<path> a toplevel share GET /<namespace> with a websocket upgrade the namespace's update stream GET /openapi.json the API description GET /seamless-client.js the browser client GET / 302 to /index.html when such a top-level share exists, else 404 GET /<namespace>/ 302 to /<namespace>/index.html when that share exists, else 404 OPTIONS anything the CORS preflight answer openapi.json , seamless-client.js and every claimed or held namespace name are reserved top-level keys; a namespace cannot take the name of an existing top-level share. state-graph is a reserved namespace key: a non-top-level share with that exact path raises ValueError . A top-level share named state-graph remains legal. A key is matched whole: there is no access below a share. A download and a share are keys of the same namespace: they cannot have the same key. The state graph Once a Context has its first share, GET /<namespace>/state-graph serves its whole node state graph until the Context closes , including after its last share is removed, and serves its last publication through the hold that follows the close ( The hold on close ). Changing the namespace after final unshare releases the old namespace and its URL; the next share establishes the new one. A Context that never shared anything has no state-graph URL. Exposure is always on: every node's path, celltype or transformer language, state, checksum and error text is served to anyone who can reach the server, including nodes whose values are not shared. The JSON object has nodes , anonymous_nodes and connections . Each named node has type , path , state , block_reason , exception and checksum ; cells additionally have celltype , transformers language . state , block_reason and exception match the bound handle's reporting. Checksums are hex strings or null. connections and anonymous_nodes have exactly the graph-format structure written by get_graph() , so node identities and anonymous source references can be resolved in the same way. {"nodes":[{"type":"cell","path":["a"],"celltype":"plain","state":"complete","block_reason":null,"exception":null,"checksum":"<hex>"},{"type":"transformer","path":["add"],"language":"python","state":"blocked","block_reason":{"a":"blocked-by-error"},"exception":null,"checksum":null}],"anonymous_nodes":{},"connections":[{"type":"connection","source":["a"],"target":["add","a"]}]} The payload omits transformer code and configuration, per-pin states and the run ledger (generation, hold deadlines and superseded runs). It never resolves values or buffers, performs derivation or computes a result. The digest is the SHA-256 of canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators). It is a change token only; the body is not stored in the buffer cache or hashserver. The marker increases only when the published digest changes. It is monotonic per namespace for the lifetime of the server: a Context that takes over a held namespace continues the sequence, and its first publication is announced only if its digest differs from the held one. A client resets its state-graph marker memory on reconnect ( seamless-client.js ). GET and HEAD answer 200 application/json , with ETag: "<digest>" , X-Seamless-Marker and Cache-Control: no-cache . If-None-Match matching the digest answers 304 . HEAD omits the body. PUT answers 405 ; an unavailable Context, or a namespace that is neither claimed nor held, answers 404 ; a refresh timeout answers 503 . During a hold, GET and HEAD answer the closed Context's last publication, or 404 if it never published one. At most one snapshot is built per half-second per Context , regardless of request rate. A snapshot may be up to one interval old. A GET reuses a publication younger than the interval, and refreshes an older dirty publication or the first publication. A connected namespace client requests a dirty refresh each interval; a clean Context returns the cached publication without a controller turn. Without websocket clients or GET requests, no snapshot work runs. Snapshot reads run on the controller thread as read turns, and never poison the Context on failure. Standard graphs of a few hundred nodes require a single small pass over nodes and edges, without copying transformer configuration. The record and the marker The served state of a share is a record : a checksum, or none, and a marker . The marker is an integer that increases by one every time the served checksum changes , by a delivery from the cell or by an accepted PUT. It is monotonic per URL for the lifetime of the server , across unshare, re-share and a hold. It restarts with the process, so a marker lower than one already seen at the same URL means that the server process restarted. The browser client relies on this ( seamless-client.js ). The record holds a claim on the served checksum , so a value that was resolvable when it was announced stays resolvable while it is served, through a hold included. Reading: GET and HEAD The body is the buffer of the served checksum, byte for byte. There is no share-local serialization, so the SHA-256 of the body is the checksum in the ETag . Status When 200 the value; headers Content-Type , ETag: "<checksum hex>" , X-Seamless-Marker: <n> , Cache-Control: no-cache 204 the value is null ; ETag and X-Seamless-Marker as above, no body 304 If-None-Match names the served checksum 404 no such share, or the share has no value yet; the JSON body says which 503 the value's bytes cannot be resolved ?mode=checksum returns the checksum hex as text/plain instead of the value. HEAD never resolves bytes ; it answers from the record. A GET resolves; it never computes. It has exactly the powers of .buffer : the local buffer cache, then this process's local buffer sources, then the remote buffer server. A value whose checksum arrived without its bytes — a remote result, a cache hit, a scratch result that was evicted — answers 503 until the bytes become resolvable ( contracts/attachments.md , A delivery resolves; it never computes ). Without a hashserver, a shared cell does not take a checksum whose buffer is missing. A cache hit, typically after a value went X → Y → X and X's buffer expired, leaves the cell waiting while the Context fingertips the buffer. Until it is recovered, the share keeps serving its last value under its marker, and no update message is sent. Then the new checksum is served and announced as an ordinary update ( contracts/workflow-context.md , A Context without a hashserver ). The GET itself still never fingertips. It answers 503 for such a value only if the fingertip failed. Only complete values are served. While the cell is waiting , blocked or failed , the share keeps answering with the last value it served, under the same marker. Before the first complete value it answers 404 , unless the share re-attached a held record: it then keeps answering with the held value, under the held marker ( The hold on close ). The node state graph reports the current state separately ( The state graph ). Content types The content type is the first of: the mimetype argument; for a text or bytes cell, the type guessed from the extension of the share path ( index.html , logo.png ); the celltype's default: Celltype Content type text text/plain python , ipython text/x-python yaml application/yaml plain , str , int , float , bool application/json bytes , binary , mixed application/octet-stream charset=utf-8 is added to text/* . A str cell serves a quoted JSON string; use text for raw text. Writing: PUT The request body is the value, in the cell's celltype — the bytes a file mount would read for the same cell. Status When 200 accepted; JSON {"checksum": "<hex>", "marker": <n>} — the record after the write 400 a malformed marker or mode parameter 404 no such share; or a held share whose hold window ended before it was re-attached ( The hold on close ) 405 the share is read-only; Allow: GET, HEAD 409 ?marker=n does not equal the current marker; JSON {"checksum", "marker"} of the record 413 the body exceeds the request limit 422 the body is not a value of the celltype; JSON {"error": "<reason>"} 503 the Context did not process the write within the wait limit ( Limits ); for a PUT to a held share, the wait for the re-attach counts The body is canonicalized with canon_T , and checked exactly as a user assignment of the same value is checked — the rule of contracts/mounts.md , Canonical bytes , including that code celltypes get no syntax check. The cell holds the canonical bytes: a GET after a PUT of {"a":1} to a plain cell returns the canonical serialization. An empty body, or null , writes null. An invalid body is refused and changes nothing. It is an invalid request, not an invalid resource: the cell keeps its value and its state. A share never puts a sense error on its cell. ?marker=n makes the write conditional : n is the marker the client last saw, and the PUT is accepted only if it still is the current one. Without the parameter the PUT is unconditional. A PUT of the value already served is accepted and changes nothing : 200 , with the unchanged marker. An accepted PUT is a sensed write ( contracts/attachments.md , Sense ): a non-detaching authoritative write, with no privilege over a user assignment and none under it. The 200 is sent after the write has been installed. A ctx.a.checksum read, or a ctx.compute() , that starts after the response sees the PUT value or a newer one. A PUT to a held share waits until the share is re-attached ( The hold on close ), and is then processed as a PUT to the re-attached share, after that share's initial decision. If the decision changed the served value, a ?marker= condition fails with 409 ; if the share is now read-only, the answer is 405 ; if the window ends first, 404 . Every websocket client is told at acceptance , before the cell has taken the value, and without delivery pacing. A PUT beats a delivery that is in flight. The delivery is acknowledged as a conflict, and the cell takes the PUT value. Cell to share Delivery follows contracts/attachments.md , Actuate , without exception. A delivery moves a checksum, never bytes. It updates the record and announces it; nothing is resolved until a client asks. Intermediate values are not queued , and delivery starts are paced per session ( contracts/attachments.md , Actuate ): a rapidly changing cell is announced as its latest value. A value sensed from a PUT is not delivered back. The record already holds it. The initial decision The initial decision is the table of contracts/mounts.md , The initial decision table , read with the served value in the place of the file , with authority="cell" , and with a new share as an absent file . Share Cell Result read-only complete , value N N is served before share() returns read-only no complete value nothing is served until the cell completes writable complete , value N N is served before share() returns writable no complete value cell ← null , and null is served The last row is row 4 of the no-value table and not a share rule: an absent resource attached in a sensing mode to a cell without a value installs null. Give the cell a value before sharing it when null is not wanted. A share that re-attaches to a held record makes the same decision ( The hold on close ): the held record counts as an absent file and never writes to the cell. It only gives the served side a starting point. A delivery of the held checksum therefore changes nothing — no marker bump, no update message — and a read-only share on a cell without a complete value keeps serving the held value until the cell completes. A writable share on a cell without a value still installs null, which is an ordinary update unless null was held. Downloads A download is an archive of cell buffers, served at one URL of the namespace and built when it is requested. An archive has no canonical serialization, so it never gets a checksum: it is not a cell value, it never enters the buffer cache, and only a GET builds it. Its use case is a page button that downloads a section of the Context. url = ctx.shares.add_download(["title", "results/table"], format="zip") # "http://<host>:<port>/<namespace>/download" add_download(cells, path="download", *, format="tar.gz") blocks until the URL answers, and returns it. path is a key of the namespace under the rules of a share key ( The API ). A download is never top-level. cells names cells by path string, with / between path segments : "results/table" is ctx.results.table . In a list, each path string is also the name of its archive member; a dict {member: cell} names the members explicitly. Only cells are named: a subcontext path does not stand for the cells below it. Before a GET, only syntax is checked. A cell path is a non-empty sequence of share-key segments whose first segment is not shares . Member names follow the same segment rule; they are distinct, and none is a directory prefix of another ( a and a/b ). Whether a path names a cell is decided by each GET, never before: a download does not follow the graph, and no graph edit changes or refuses a download. format is "tar" , "tar.gz" , "tar.xz" or "zip" . It fixes the content type and the file name. remove_download(path="download") removes the URL at once. For a path without a download it is a no-op. ctx.shares.downloads is this Context's {path: DownloadSpec} . For the namespace, URL conflicts, the server start, the state graph and the hold, a download counts as a share ( Namespaces , URL space , The hold on close ). Without a hashserver, a cell that a download lists does not take a checksum whose buffer is missing , as for a shared cell ( contracts/workflow-context.md , A Context without a hashserver ). The cell is waiting while the Context fingertips the buffer, and a GET answers 409 with the reason waiting meanwhile. For a folder cell the fingertip also regenerates missing leaves. Nothing keeps those leaves afterwards: once they are evicted, a GET answers 503 . A w file mount on the folder keeps it downloadable , because its written files are a local buffer source for the leaves. The user adds that mount; the Context does not. The download GET A GET takes one consistent cut of the cells, then resolves and packs their buffers. The cut is one read turn of the Context. Every listed path is looked up in the same turn, so an archive never mixes two states of the graph. The turn reads checksums; it never computes, and it claims every checksum it read until the archive is built. Every listed path must name a complete cell whose celltype is not deep. Otherwise the answer is 409 , with JSON {"error": "<message>", "cells": {"<cell path>": "<reason>", …}} that lists every failing path. The reasons are missing (no node and no subcontext at that path), not-a-cell (a transformer or a subcontext), deep-celltype ( deepcell , deepfolder ), and otherwise the node state: unwired , miswired , blocked , waiting , computing or failed . Members are buffers. A member's bytes are the cell's buffer, byte for byte: the body a share GET would answer for that cell ( Reading: GET and HEAD ). A folder cell becomes a directory, with one member <member>/<key> per index entry, holding that leaf's buffer; an index key that is not a safe relative path fails the cut with the reason unsafe-folder-key . A cell whose value is null is left out , and so is a null folder leaf. Buffers are resolved with the powers of a share GET, never computed; a buffer that cannot be resolved answers 503 . Packing is deterministic : members in sorted order, a fixed timestamp (tar: 0; zip: 1980-01-01 00:00), owner 0, mode 0644 , and a gzip header without file name or time. With a given compression library, two GETs of the same cut return the same bytes. The archive is still not content-addressed. Status When 200 the archive; headers Content-Type and Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>" ( below ), Cache-Control: no-cache 404 no such download; or a held download whose hold window ended before it was re-attached ( The hold on close ) 405 any method but GET ; Allow: GET, OPTIONS 409 the cut has failing paths; the JSON body lists every one with its reason 503 a buffer cannot be resolved; the Context did not answer the read; the build exceeded its time limit ( Limits ) format Content-Type file name tar application/x-tar <last path segment>.tar tar.gz application/gzip <last path segment>.tar.gz tar.xz application/x-xz <last path segment>.tar.xz zip application/zip <last path segment>.zip The extension is not added when the last path segment already ends with it: path="report.zip" is served as report.zip . A download has no record. There is no ETag , no X-Seamless-Marker and no ?mode=checksum , and the websocket never lists or announces a download. Downloads are built on a worker pool of their own , so a slow build never delays a share GET or a state-graph read. The websocket GET /<namespace> with a websocket upgrade opens the namespace's update stream. The server only sends; anything a client sends is ignored. Every message is a JSON array. ["Seamless share update server", "1.0"] — once, first. ["shares", {<key>: {"url": "/ctx/a", "readonly": true, "content_type": "application/json", "binary": false, "checksum": "<hex>" | null, "marker": 3}, …}] — the full state, after the handshake and again whenever a share is added to or removed from the namespace, or re-attached with a different readonly , content_type or binary ( The hold on close ). It includes the namespace's top-level shares. ["update", [<key>, "<checksum hex>", <marker>]] — on every change of a record. ["state-graph", ["<digest>", <marker>]] — announces a state graph publication; GET the state-graph URL for its body. A client needs no request to learn the current state : the first shares message carries every checksum and marker. Downloads are not listed : they have no record, so they have no update either. Adding or removing a download sends no shares message. A new client receives its first state-graph announcement within one half-second interval after the initial share snapshot. Further announcements arrive at most once per interval and only when the published digest differs from the last digest sent to that client. Changes that return to the previously published graph inside one interval produce no announcement. binary is false for text/* , application/json , application/yaml , application/javascript , application/xml and the +json / +xml types, and true otherwise. Liveness uses websocket ping frames, not a message. A Context close does not close the connections. They are held with the namespace and pass to the Context that takes it over ( The hold on close ). They are closed with code 1001 when the namespace is released — at the end of a hold that no Context took over, or when its owner changes namespace after its final unshare — and when the server stops. openapi.json GET /openapi.json returns an OpenAPI 3.1 document generated from the shares that exist at the moment of the request, held shares included, for every namespace. ctx.shares.openapi() returns the same document restricted to one Context, and shareserver.openapi() the whole one, without a request. One state-graph path item per claimed or held namespace , with GET and HEAD and the responses described in The state graph . One path item per share , at its URL: get and head always, put when the share is writable, with the status codes of this page. One path item per download , at its URL: get only, answering the archive content type, with x-seamless-download holding {"format", "cells"} . Content type and schema follow the celltype: Celltype Schema int {"type": "integer"} float {"type": "number"} bool {"type": "boolean"} str {"type": "string"} plain {} — any JSON text , python , ipython , yaml {"type": "string"} bytes , binary , mixed binary content, no schema PUT request schemas additionally accept null, and the request body is optional because an omitted or empty body writes null ( Writing: PUT ). GET value schemas remain as listed above; mode=checksum additionally returns text/plain checksum text. A mimetype argument replaces the content type; the schema is then a string for text types and binary otherwise. Each operation carries x-seamless-celltype and x-seamless-node (the node path). The websocket is described in info.description and by x-seamless-updates ( {"<namespace>": "/<namespace>"} ); OpenAPI itself cannot express it. Individual value endpoints describe only shared cells; the state-graph endpoint includes all named cells and transformers. seamless-client.js GET /seamless-client.js serves a dependency-free browser client. It needs no share of its own. const ctx = connect_seamless() // same origin, namespace "ctx" ctx.self.onsharelist = function (keys) { ctx.a.onchange = function () { show(ctx.a.value) } } ctx.a.set("5") // PUT connect_seamless(update_server=null, rest_server=null, share_namespace="ctx") . The first two arguments name the one server and are aliases; null means the page's own origin. Each accepts a port number or a URL. If both are given and differ, the second wins and a warning is logged. One entry per share whose mapped property is distinct and is not self , ctx[<key>] with / written as __ : value , checksum , marker , binary , content_type , readonly , auto_read , set(value) , oninput , onchange . ctx.self holds sharelist , onsharelist , oninput , onchange , get_value() , connect() , ws , server , share_namespace , stategraph and onstategraph . The property-mapping limitation is listed under Implementation status and current limitations . value is text, or a Blob when the share is binary ; null for a null value. JSON is not parsed for you. auto_read is false for keys containing a . — pages, scripts, images — and true otherwise; only auto-read shares are fetched on change. set() sends one PUT per key at a time , conditional on the marker it last saw, and keeps only the latest value set meanwhile. On 409 the client drops the local change, adopts the record in the response and fetches the server's value. A record or value whose marker is lower than the client's own is adopted only once the client has concluded that the server restarted (below); before that, it is ignored. Entries survive a new shares message : handlers stay attached, and only added and removed keys change. ctx.self.onstategraph enables state graph reads. When set, an announcement triggers a GET of /<namespace>/state-graph ; the parsed object is stored in ctx.self.stategraph , then the handler is called. Responses older than the newest marker seen are dropped, and marker memory resets on reconnect. Pages without the handler do no extra reads. A lost connection is retried with backoff. A Context close loses no connection: the connection is held and passes to the Context that takes over the namespace ( The hold on close ). The first shares message after a reconnect tells a restarted server from the same one ( The record and the marker ): Restarted : a server marker is lower than the client's, for a key the client holds, beyond one tolerated not-yet-processed PUT in total . The snapshot may predate the processing of a PUT whose response the client already has, because the HTTP response can overtake the websocket. So when exactly one key is lower, by exactly one, and the client's marker for that key comes from the response to its own PUT, that is no evidence of a restart; any other lower marker is. On a restart, the client adopts the server's marker for every key it holds and reads no value : its values and checksums stand, and no oninput or onchange is called. Mounted cells were restored from their files, so the page's own state is taken to be current; if it is not, the user reloads the page. Keys new to the client, and keys whose value it never read, are read as on a first connection. So is every key whose dropped change the client could not correct, because it ignored a 409 record with a lower marker ( set() above). Same server : no marker is lower beyond that tolerance. The client adopts every server marker and checksum that is not lower than its own, and re-reads every auto-read share. The update for a tolerated PUT follows on the websocket. A write that reaches a restarted server before the client has adopted its markers carries a marker of the previous process and is normally refused with 409 , and the client drops the change. If it has not concluded the restart yet, it ignores the response's record and the value it then reads, both carrying a lower marker ( set() above): the page keeps showing the dropped change until the reconnect, when the client concludes the restart and reads that key. The barrier ctx.mounts.sync() cuts share sessions like any other. A cut reports after every PUT accepted before it has been processed. Its SyncReport and ctx.mounts.errors carry an entry per share under the key (node_path, "share") . ctx.compute() stays graph-only , but because a PUT answers after its write is installed, a script that PUTs — from another thread or another process — and then computes needs no barrier in between. Threads and blocking Every public call is an ordinary public Context operation. share() , del ctx.a.share , clear_error() , add_download() , remove_download() and setting ctx.shares.namespace block the caller, raise ReentrantContextError from the controller thread and ClosedContextError after close() . Request handlers run on the server thread. No user code runs in them. A download is built on a worker thread of the download pool; its cut is one read turn of the Context. A blocking HTTP call from the thread that owns the Context is fine : the server does not need that thread. Errors Raised at the call: Error Raised when AttributeError("share is only available for bound workflow cells") a standalone Cell AttributeError("Only whole Context cell nodes can be shared") a sub-path projection ( ctx.a.b ); a read-only handle, including a transformer's result, ctx.tf.result NodeError("Shares require an existing whole cell node") the node does not exist or is not a cell ValueError("Cell is already shared; unshare first") the share slot is occupied ValueError("Share path '<path>' is in use") another share of the namespace, or another top-level share, has the key — a held top-level share included, for every Context but the one that takes over its namespace; or the key is reserved ValueError("Share namespace '<name>' is in use") another live Context has claimed the namespace ValueError an invalid key; an unparseable mimetype ; a top-level key with more than one segment TypeError("Celltype '<ct>' is not shareable") Shareable celltypes AuthorityError("A writable share cannot have incoming edges; share it read-only") readonly=False on a connected cell AuthorityError an incoming edge into a writably shared cell; clearing a shared cell OSError the server cannot bind ImportError aiohttp is not installed ( seamless-workflow[share] ) ValueError for add_download() : an invalid download path, cell path or member name; two members with one name; a member name that is a directory prefix of another; an unknown format ; a download path taken by a share or a download, as for a share TypeError for add_download() : cells is neither a list of strings nor a dict of strings add_download() never raises because of the graph: a path that names no cell, or a cell that is not complete, is reported by the GET ( The download GET ). The remedy for every scope refusal is the usual one: share a cell and connect it. ctx.out = ctx.tf.result; ctx.out.share() serves a transformer's result. Of the three-way error model of contracts/attachments.md , a share has only the delivery error , on ctx.a.share.error : the server could not take the delivery. It is retried with the usual backoff. There is no sense error ( Writing: PUT ), and the oscillation detector cannot trip: a read-only share has no foreign writer, and a writable one never reasserts. Graph serialization Format 0.7 adds the top-level downloads list; 0.6 added the share entry. 0.2 to 0.6 graphs load. A share entry in a graph below 0.6 raises PathError("share entries require workflow graph version 0.6") , and a downloads list in a graph below 0.7 raises PathError("downloads require workflow graph version 0.7") . The share entry is {"path", "readonly", "mimetype", "toplevel"} on a cell entry — the spec after normalization, with the default key written out. A download entry is {"path", "cells", "format"} , sorted by path . cells is a list when every member is named after its cell, else a {member: cell} dict. A graph without downloads has no downloads key. Every share entry is validated by prepare_graph , also with shares=False : unknown fields, an invalid key, an unshareable celltype, a share on a non-cell node, a connection into a writably shared node, and two shares with one URL are refused as PathError("Invalid share spec: …") . Every download entry is validated by the same syntax rules as add_download() , and no more : unknown fields, invalid paths or names, two downloads with one path, and a download with the key of a share are refused as PathError("Invalid download spec: …") . Cell paths are not checked against the graph. shares=False strips the (valid) share specs and downloads. shares=True — the default — attaches every spec exactly as share() does, and registers every download exactly as add_download() does. It starts the server if needed, and it blocks through every first delivery, like mounts=True . A key or namespace that is taken raises, and the graph is not replaced. The downloads of the previous graph are removed, except where a new download or share takes over their key. The namespace is not in the graph. Set ctx.shares.namespace before loading. Loading a graph with shares or downloads opens a network endpoint. Graphs of unknown origin must be loaded with shares=False . Serving saved graphs The seamless-suite distribution installs seamless-serve-graph , whose entry point is seamless_workflow.serve_graph:main , and includes seamless-workflow[share] . seamless-serve-graph graph.json The command takes exactly one local graph file. It reads UTF-8 JSON and passes it to the current workflow graph loader. The graph must use the current workflow serialization; the command does not convert an original legacy __seamless__ export. Share entries require workflow graph version 0.6 . The Context uses its default ctx namespace. Shares in the saved graph become URLs under /ctx/ ; top-level shares keep their declared paths. The runner restores shares and disables file mounts. It does not require the graph to declare a share. Loading starts reactive derivation. The runner does not perform a buffer-availability preflight. Its share server uses the ordinary modern HTTP/websocket protocol and bind configuration from seamless_workflow.shareserver . The runner owns shutdown. It waits for SIGINT or SIGTERM in the main thread, restores the previous signal handlers, closes the Context, and calls seamless.close() . Remote storage and execution use seamless-config . Define the cluster and execution mode in the normal Seamless configuration files before launch. The runner loads configuration relative to its launch directory and has no remote-service flags. See Setting up a local cluster and Remote execution . Lifecycle Every detach removes the URL at once, except a Context close. del ctx.a.share , deleting the node, an empty same-celltype builder and set_graph() all end in the same detach ( contracts/attachments.md , Attach, detach, close ). Requests then answer 404 , and the namespace's clients get a new shares message. remove_download() and set_graph() remove a download's URL at once ; requests then answer 404 . Deleting or changing a cell never touches a download. ctx.close() holds its shares , and removes at the end of the hold window those that no new Context re-attached ( The hold on close ). Slot detach is independent. del ctx.a.share leaves a file mount and a widget hub in place. A new share on the same URL continues its marker sequence. To change path , readonly , mimetype or toplevel , unshare and share again. del ctx.a.share on a cell without a share is a no-op, and .spec , .url , .status and .error answer None . The hold on close ctx.close() does not remove its shares at once. The server holds them for a window, 10 s by default ( Limits ), and a Context that shares the same URLs inside the window takes them over. Re-running a serving script with %run -i — close the old Context, build a new one — is therefore invisible to clients for every value that did not change. What is held is the namespace : every record of the closing Context, top-level ones included, each with its entry, checksum, marker and claim; its downloads; the websocket connections; and the last state-graph publication. A Context that never claimed a namespace holds nothing. A held download is never built : the Context that defined it is closed. A GET to a held download waits until a share or download is re-attached at its URL, and is then answered by it, as a PUT to a held share is ( Writing: PUT ); if the window ends first, it answers 404 . The hold starts when close() stops sensing ( contracts/attachments.md , Close , step 1). The close flush still completes the deliveries already requested, as ordinary updates. After the flush, nothing the closing Context does changes a record or sends a message: its teardown is invisible. The window starts when close() returns ; close() does not wait for it. During the hold, held shares answer from their records. GET, HEAD and ?mode=checksum answer as before, and the connections stay open. A client that connects gets the handshake, a shares message with the held records and, if there is one, an announcement of the held state-graph publication, which the state-graph URL serves. /openapi.json keeps describing the held shares and the namespace's state-graph endpoint. A PUT waits for its share to be re-attached ( Writing: PUT ). The first Context that claims the namespace inside the window takes it over — by its first share, or by a set_graph() that attaches shares — instead of raising ValueError("Share namespace '<name>' is in use") . The connections, the held records and the state-graph marker sequence pass to it. The held top-level keys are refused to every other Context. A share or download of that Context at the URL of a held record or download re-attaches to it , whatever its node, celltype, flags or kind. A download takes nothing from what it re-attaches to; a share that re-attaches to a held download starts as a new share. A shares message is sent when a share replaces a download or the reverse. Its initial decision is that of a new share, and the held record only gives the served side its starting point ( The initial decision ): a value equal to the held one is served under the held marker: no marker bump, no update message; a different value is one ordinary update; a read-only share on a cell without a complete value keeps serving the held value until the cell completes; a writable one installs null, which is an ordinary update unless null was held; a shares message is sent only if readonly , content_type or binary changed. A held record that is not re-attached by the end of its window is removed , as by any detach: requests answer 404 , a waiting PUT answers 404 , and the namespace's clients get a new shares message. If no Context took the namespace over, the namespace is released with its records: its connections are closed with code 1001 , and its URLs, the state-graph URL included, answer 404 . A Context that took over a namespace holds it again when it closes. Its own records, re-attached ones included, get a new window; records still held from the earlier close keep theirs. Only ctx.close() holds. Every other detach removes the URL at once ( Lifecycle ). seamless.close() stops the server, which ends every hold. A hold never feeds a Context. A value that a browser wrote into an unmounted cell does not reach the new Context, which starts from its own script. State that must survive a reload belongs in a file mount ( contracts/mounts.md ). Limits The numbers are current defaults, not contract: Knob Current default request body limit 1 GiB wait for a PUT to be installed 60 s, then 503 resolution timeout of a GET 60 s, then 503 websocket ping interval 10 s hold window after ctx.close() 10 s time to build a download, cut included 300 s, then 503 download worker pool 2 threads delivery pacing contracts/attachments.md , Actuate A value is held in memory in full for the duration of a request, and so is a download archive. There are no range requests. Porting notes Stated as current behaviour, with no claim about what any earlier version did: There is one port , for REST and websocket. Bodies are values. A PUT body is the value itself, and so is a GET body; there is no JSON envelope and no base64. ?marker= is the marker you last saw , not the one you propose. A websocket client gets the current state on connect. Null is 204 . 404 means there is no value. A GET never recomputes a value. share() returns None . The content type is an argument of share() , or follows the path's extension or the celltype. The namespace is set on the Context at run time , and a taken name raises. A busy port raises. The client is served by the server , at /seamless-client.js . ctx.compute() does not wait for shares , and does not need to after a PUT has answered. Implementation status and current limitations The share API, HTTP/WebSocket server, persistence, OpenAPI description and browser client implement this contract. Focused tests in seamless-workflow/tests/test_contract_shares.py , test_share_transport.py , test_share_client_js.py and test_share_downloads.py pin the behavior. Browser acceptance passed against headless Chrome in seamless-workflow/tests/test_share_browser.py , including slider keyboard input, Python-to-browser updates, two-tab editing and mounted-page updates. Topology refusals raised by generic code say "mount". An incoming edge into a writably shared cell raises AuthorityError("Sensing mount is the producer; unmount first") , and clearing raises AuthorityError("Cannot clear a mounted cell; unmount first") . The remedy is del ctx.a.share . The barrier is spelled ctx.mounts . A writable share cannot be made on a cell that should stay empty ( The initial decision ). The browser client's property mapping cannot represent every legal share key. a/b and a__b both map to ctx.a__b , and self collides with the client control API. These remain valid HTTP share paths. For a namespace containing such keys, choose distinct share paths or use the HTTP endpoints through a custom client. Non-goals Generating a web page or form from the graph. A page is a text cell that you write and share. Access below a share ( /ctx/a/x ). Share a connected cell that holds the projection: ctx.x = ctx.a.x; ctx.x.share() . PUT by checksum. Deferred with a named condition: it needs the check that ctx.a.checksum = … performs, which a transport cannot perform today. Directory and deep shares. folder , deepfolder and deepcell cells are not shareable. A folder cell can be downloaded ( Downloads ); deepfolder and deepcell cells cannot. Downloads of computed content. A download packs buffers of complete cells; it runs no user code. Content that must be computed for the archive, such as a manifest, belongs in a cell. Computing on GET. A GET resolves and never fingertips. Without a hashserver, the Context fingertips a shared cell's missing buffer before the share receives the checksum, never during a request ( Reading: GET and HEAD ). Authentication, TLS, sessions. Every client of a namespace edits the same graph. Use a reverse proxy for access control, and one Context per user for isolation. Standalone, sub-path, pin and code shares. As for every attachment ( contracts/attachments.md , Non-goals ).

docs.text: A share is the attachment whose external resource is an HTTP endpoint served by this process. The cell's value is read with GET, written with PUT when the share is writable, and every change is announced over a websocket. The attachment contract of contracts/attachments.md applies in full — direction, scope, slots, spec versus session, the sense and actuate disciplines, delivery pacing, the cut barrier and the lifecycle. This page specializes it for values served over HTTP. It does not restate a rule from that page; each section says where the share driver makes a generic rule concrete. The same server also serves downloads : archives of cell buffers, each at one URL of the namespace, built when they are requested ( Downloads ). A download is not an attachment; it belongs to the Context, not to a cell. Only in a Context without a hashserver does a listed cell count as attached, and only for the fingertip before an update ( Downloads ). Shares exist on the workflow Context only. A standalone Cell and a direct / delayed transformer have no HTTP integration. The seamless-serve-graph command loads workflow Contexts with their declared shares and downloads ( Serving saved graphs below). A share is unrelated to the seamless-share package , which inspects and exports cached buffers and transformations. Code locations: Concern Module / symbol Public handles seamless_workflow.attachments.share.api ( ShareHandle , ContextShares ) Server configuration seamless_workflow.shareserver ( configure , host , port , url , openapi , close ) Durable spec, celltype admission seamless_workflow.attachments.share.spec ( ShareSpec , DownloadSpec , validate_celltype ) Download cut seamless_workflow.attachments.runtime.AttachmentRuntime._download_cut Archive packing seamless_workflow.attachments.share.archive Transport seamless_workflow.attachments.share.driver.ShareDriver Server, records, namespaces, holds seamless_workflow.attachments.share.server ( ShareServer ) Content types seamless_workflow.attachments.share.mime API description seamless_workflow.attachments.share.openapi Browser client seamless_workflow/attachments/share/static/seamless-client.js Cell handle seamless.cell_class.Cell.share (property plus deleter, seamless-core) Session protocol, policy, barrier as in contracts/attachments.md
